LESSON: WRITING 3.5.1 ELEMENTS OF EFFECTIVE WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.5: Writing 3.5.1 Elements of effective writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.5.1 Elements of effective writing, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we organise ideas logically in writing? 2. How do connectors help in interpreting information?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the use of addition, similarity and contrast connectors in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.5.1 Elements of effective writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use addition, contrast, and similarity connectors in paragraphs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.5.1 Elements of effective writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. order ideas in a paragraph for coherence,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.5.1 Elements of effective writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. write a coherent paragraph on a given topic, ● in pairs, learners are guided to identify connectors of addition, similarity and contrast from a text, ● in groups, learners with low vision are guided to use pictorials while learners with blindness write a summary to sequentially order events from a narrative, 1.    In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. acknowledge the value of logically ordering ideas in writing. ● in pairs, learners are guided to collaborate and rearrange disordered sentences from word cards to form a logical paragraph, ● in groups, learners are guided to team up to write a coherent paragraph on a topic around the theme.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.5.1 Elements of effective writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: The learner exhibits concerted attention to detail as they use pictorials and summary to sequentially order

events from a narrative.

● Problem Solving: The learner follows instructions very carefully as they are guided to collaborate and rearrange disordered

sentences from word cards to form a logical paragraph.

Values:
● Unity: The learner appreciates the importance of oneness as they team up to write a coherent paragraph on a topic around

the theme.

● Respect: The learner exercises positive regard for self and others as they collaborate and rearrange disordered sentences

from word cards to form a logical paragraph.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education: The learner manifests principles of leadership as they team up to write a coherent paragraph on a topic

around the theme.

39

● Print texts

● Braille texts

● Electronic reading materials

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Suggested Skills:

● Explaining the use of addition, similarity and contrast connectors in a text,

● Using addition, contrast, and similarity connectors in paragraphs,

● Ordering ideas in a paragraph for coherence,

● Writing a coherent paragraph on a given topic,
